# Dropping a file into a location to start work

The bundled `sensor-object-store` service lists a designated location and hands
each newly deposited object to the graph as a message. The producing side writes
no integration code; it drops the file.

## Wire the sensor

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db
claim_producers: {}
named_locks: {}
executors: {}
publishers:
  "inbox":
    endpoint: "object-store-sensor:9083"
    protocols: ["publisher"]
```

The filesystem backend is designated by one setting:

```bash
docker run -d --network rimsky-net --network-alias object-store-sensor \
  -e RIMSKY_SENSOR_OBJECT_STORE_PORT=9083 \
  -e RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL=http://rimsky:8080 \
  -e RIMSKY_SENSOR_OBJECT_STORE_FS_ROOT=/data \
  -v "$PWD/inbox:/data:ro" \
  rimsky-sensor-object-store:<tag>
```

## The template

```json
{
  "name": "object-store-demo",
  "version": "1",
  "messages": [{"type": "drop/arrived"}],
  "nodes": [{
    "type": "handler",
    "kind": "attribute_passthrough",
    "subscribes": [{"node": "drop/arrived", "type": "terminal/success",
                    "force_upstream_refresh": false}],
    "attributes": {"schema": {"type": "object",
                              "properties": {"v": {"type": "integer", "default": 1}}}}
  }],
  "publishers": [{
    "name": "inbox", "kind": "object-store", "message_type": "drop/arrived",
    "config": {"backend": "filesystem", "bucket": "inbox", "prefix": "in/",
               "poll_interval": "1s", "watermark_field": "name"}
  }]
}
```

## Deposit a file

```bash
cp report.csv ./inbox/in/report.csv

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages"
```

A publisher message arrives naming the backend, the bucket, the object name, its
size, its content hash and its modification time. The subscribed node runs on
it.

No operator message is posted at any point.

## Only the designated location counts

A file deposited outside the `in/` prefix produces no message. A file deposited
under the prefix afterwards still does — the later arrival shows the sensor kept
listing the location rather than reading it once at startup.

The operator's designation bounds what enters the graph; neighbouring content in
the same store stays out of it.

## Each object exactly once

Deposit three objects under the prefix. The graph sees three messages for three
objects, none handed over twice, and the subscribed node runs three times.

Each deposit drives its own run rather than being folded into a batch, so a
producer dropping several objects gets several units of work and no duplicates.
